Give an exploration its own Study Tracker ID

Source: R/study_promote.R
study_promote.Rd

An exploration set up with study_setup(derived_from = ) has a provisional_id and no Study Tracker ID of its own. Once the Tracker has registered it, study_promote() writes that ID into _study.yml and removes provisional_id. derived_from and workspace_id stay, so the lineage to the parent study is kept. When the study has a checkpoint repository and a remote, the checkpoints held locally while the study was provisional are delivered at once, with the study_promoted checkpoint described below, and study_checkpoint_push retries anything still pending; their tags are unchanged. Checkpoint commits and tag messages made while the study was provisional keep the provisional ID; they are pushed unchanged.

Usage

study_promote(study_tracker_id, start = ".")

Arguments

study_tracker_id

The study's new Study Tracker ID, one positive integer.

start

A directory in the study. The study is found as by study_config.

Value

The number of checkpoint entries rewritten, invisibly; the study_promoted checkpoint is not counted. A rerun after an interrupted promotion rewrites the entries again, and the provisional ID already recorded is kept. A study that is already promoted, or whose _study.yml still has a legacy st_id key, is refused, as is one whose checkpoint repository is not on main. A rerun with a different ID rewrites every entry to it.

Details

When the study has a checkpoint repository, study_promote() then records a study_promoted checkpoint: a snapshot of the promoted study, tagged study_promoted, and delivers it with the held checkpoints, printing the usual delivery messages, so the promoted _study.yml reaches the remote and a second copy of the study reads it as promoted. Without a remote it stays pending until study_checkpoint_push. A study with no checkpoint repository yet takes no snapshot; its first checkpoint carries the promoted manifest. With a repository, git must be available and the study_promoted kind must not be retired; both are checked before anything is written. The study_promoted snapshot is taken whatever trigger or numbering the live vocabulary gives the kind; only retirement refuses it.

If the snapshot fails, _study.yml and the outbox stay promoted and study_promote() stops with the error. A rerun is refused, because the study is already promoted; record the checkpoint by hand instead, with study_checkpoint("study_promoted"), which is refused too if the kind has been retired.

If two copies of a study both promote, their unnumbered study_promoted tags clash on push and the second stays pending, as workspace_created does.

See also

study_setup, study_update_identity

Examples

root <- file.path(tempdir(), "promote-example")
invisible(study_setup(root, study = "Example exploration",
                      derived_from = 1L, renv = FALSE))
study_promote(2L, start = root)
unlink(root, recursive = TRUE)
